items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: I just couldn’t relate to it emotionally you know. But it went into my body. I think I understood it later.

ctx.x: In the ‘50s, were you at all attracted to bop and the kind of explosion that was occurring with that music?

I would have to say that from my own emotional understanding that the swing music say of Roy Eldridge, Coleman Hawkins and that kind of thing would have been sort of like the cutting edge for me, even though Bird and Monk and so forth were already out there changing things. When I heard Parker with the Jazz at the Philharmonic, you see there wasn’t too many, it was very hard to get into the clubs as a kid, but you could go to these concerts like Jazz at the Philharmonic. And that’s where I heard Parker and I just…
